messages:
nina: Heads-up: BI team wants a continuous SIEM export to their sandbox for feature analytics. They want 90d retention, tenant=all, full metadata (including user_agent, anonymized_ip). asking if we can push via export or need to proxy.
evan: @nina main concerns: 1) tenant=all + export = data residency & consent question. 2) full metadata could re-identify users; need minimization. 3) KMS: who holds the unwrap key?
priya: Prefer proxy/export-gateway pattern -> transform -> re-encrypt with BI CMK. That way we never hand out CMK unwrap rights to service accounts. Gateway should enforce field remove/tokenize rules.
otom: quick preference: do not export raw ingest index. Create a parsed, normalized view (parsed-events-v1) and expose that with column-level ACL. Export gateway can then consume that view and apply tokenization.
infra-bot: Note: parsed-events-v1 currently exists for new data; historical backfill would need a reindex job. Estimated size for 90d: ~700M docs. ETA for a staged backfill: 72h with throttling.
priya: retention tiers proposal: 30d = full metadata accessible to security; 90d = analytics view with IP tokenized; 365d = aggregate metrics only. Need privacy sign-off.
evan: For KMS: options: 1) BI CMK - allow encrypt-only from gateway, no decrypt rights. 2) Unwrap in infra service account that writes analytics snapshots encrypted to BI CMK. Every unwrap must have a ticket and 2 approvers. Prefer #2 for bulk historical joins.
nina: BI team wants ad-hoc joins on historical fields. Can we give them tokenized id mapping to re-hash for joins instead of unwrapping?
priya: Yes. Issue: join fidelity. Tokenization approach: deterministic keyed hash (HKDF with per-tenant salt) stored in lookup table; lookup itself lives in analytics sandbox and rotated quarterly. But storing mapping may be considered PII; need control.
otom: incident response flow: during incidents, forensic team needs fast unmask. propose: emergency_unmask endpoint that requires 2FA, 2 approvers (oncall + sec lead), logs KMS key-id, requester, reason, timeframe (max 8h). resulting snapshot is written to an immutable S3 prefix.
nina: Any objections to a short-lived export role instead of permanent? BI suggests permanent to avoid repeated approvals.
evan: Security + privacy prefer timeboxed role with automated attestation every 30 days. If attestation fails, role auto-revoked. Limit: query rate 5qps, no external sink allowed, exports must go through gateway only.
priya: snippet of proposed role (for infra):
```json
{
  "role": "siem_export_bi_temp",
  "scope": "parsed-events-v1",
  "fields_allowed": ["timestamp","event_type","normalized_user","user_agent","agent_version"],
  "field_munging": {"ip":"tokenize_v1","email":"redact"},
  "max_qps": "5",
  "expires_in": "30d",
  "export_allowed": "gateway-only"
}
```
infra-bot: Logged: SEC-7001 created for approval workflow. Attach privacy review before 1776543600 or role will be limited to 7d by policy.
evan: Also add monitoring: create alert on unusual export volumes >2x baseline for 15m -> auto-disable export gateway key and page infra.
otom: For KMS audit: require CMK alias in audit record, key version, principal, and signed statement of justification. Store audit to WORM bucket with 10y retention for compliance.
nina: I'll coordinate BI writeup and include sample queries and owners. tagging @privacy and linking SEC-7001.
evan: Ops: infra, please estimate reindex cost for 90d tokenization vs on-read tokenization tradeoffs. then we can pick approach.
infra-bot: Est: on-read tokenization = minimal compute + no backfill. Historical deterministic-token join will be lossy for some edge cases. Backfill + reindex = ~72h with 1.3x CPU and +2TB temp storage.
priya: Final decision path: 1) BI provides writeup + owners 2) privacy + security review masking plan 3) provision gateway + role (30d) 4) enable monitoring + emergency_unmask playbook 5) revisit permanence after 3 attestations.
nina: thanks team. i'll follow up in SEC-7001 and loop privacy. :white_check_mark:
